safety_lead_time.comparison_action: Reduce SAP safety lead time from 4.5 to 2.69 days

narrative: Material PL1__M9B56DBE exhibits smooth, stationary daily demand averaging 4,932 units across 213 observed working days, with a coefficient of variation of 43% indicating moderate but manageable variability. Lead times average 5.88 working days with moderate stability (CV 22%), meaning demand variability during the replenishment window is the dominant risk factor at 77.3% of total variance. An (r,Q) continuous-review policy is recommended with a safety stock of 13,315 units and a reorder point of 40,467 units, yielding a 95% service level while reducing total annual inventory cost by over 90% versus the current SAP configuration by consolidating small frequent orders into economically optimal batches.
warnings: SAP safety stock is 0 — material is currently unprotected against demand/lead-time variability
Capacity utilisation at 87.6% after applying optimised policy — monitor for demand spikes

research_insights.selection_rationale: Smooth demand (CV 43%) with no trend and moderate lead-time variability is the textbook case for a continuous-review (r,Q) policy. The policy triggers an order of fixed size Q whenever on-hand inventory falls to the reorder point r, providing tight stockout protection without the over-ordering cost of periodic-review systems. EOQ balances the low unit holding cost against the fixed ordering cost.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity of 50,800 units is satisfied (SS 13,315 + OQ 31,203 = 44,518 units, 87.6% utilisation). No capacity constraint binds; however, a demand spike above the 99th percentile combined with a late delivery could transiently push inventory above the modelled average — this should be monitored.
